title: Behavioral delta lab journal — attention / KV / batching
content:
Summary:
This is a working lab journal capturing end-to-end evaluation and quick triage for the runtime changes landed in Feb 2026: the new FlashAttention path (optimized kernels), the segmented/paged KV cache rollout (aka paged-KV), and an opt-in continuous request batching pipeline. Purpose is to surface behavioral deltas (quality regressions, token-level diffs), quantify them across prompt suites, and propose mitigations for model onboarding.

High-level findings (quick):
- FlashAttention: latency improved ~15–25% p50 on long-sequences; however, a small but measurable rise in short-token-level edits for instruction-following prompts (token-level edit distance +2.1% for the instr-suite). No evidence of numerical instability but a couple examples show dropped leading tokens in multi-turn contexts.
- Paged KV: overall memory footprint reduced and throughput improved for large context lengths, but we observed off-by-one recency shifts in retrieval-style prompts (the model sometimes repeated the penultimate retrieval item instead of the most recent). Exact-match on retrieval anchors dropped 3.6% on the retrieval prompt set.
- Continuous batching: improved amortized cost but introduced ~0.8% increase in truncated completions for long-generation tasks at high concurrency (rare timeouts during the tail of sequence generation).

Hypotheses to test:
1) FlashAttention kernel reorderings may change softmax rounding behavior for boundary tokens; this manifests in tokens where the probability mass is split across near-equal candidates.
2) Paged KV indexing off-by-one likely due to page boundary logic when a new page is loaded mid-generation — pointer arithmetic bug in page offset computation.
3) Continuous batching interaction with KV eviction timing can cause stale cache frames that lead to premature truncation at high concurrency.

Test matrix and hardware:
- Models: rdlw-13b-v1 (baseline), rdlw-13b-v1-quant (int8), rdlw-70b-v2 (selected tests).
- Runtime variants: (A) baseline kernels + single-page KV + no-cont-batch; (B) flash-kernel only; (C) paged-KV only; (D) cont-batch only; (E) combined (flash + paged-KV + cont-batch).
- Hardware: p4d-like (A100 40GB) emulated node and nvlsm-1 (H100) private cluster.
- Prompts: three curated suites (instruction-follow, retrieval-anchor, long-narrative-gen).
- Metrics captured: exact-match (retrieval anchors), token edit distance (instr-suite), Rouge-L and BLEU (narrative), p50/p95 latency, p99 memory, truncation-rate, per-token cross-entropy delta.

Prompt sets (examples):
- instr-suite: short instructions with follow-ups (50 prompts, includes edge cases where next-token ambiguity is high).
  Example prompt: "Rewrite the following paragraph as a concise bullet list, preserving meaning and examples. Keep numbers as numerals."
- retrieval-anchor: synthetic retrieval pattern where the last 3 items are unique ids; evaluation looks for exact mention of the last item. (60 prompts)
  Example prompt: "Given the following items: item-A1, item-B2, item-C3. What was listed most recently? Answer with only the id."
- long-narrative-gen: multi-paragraph generation tasks with 1k+ token targets (30 prompts)

Evaluation method:
- Each prompt run 5 seeds per runtime variant; deterministic sampling where possible (top-k/temperature fixed) for diffs.
- We store raw tokens and token-level probabilities for side-by-side diffs. The eval harness computes token edit distance, top-token delta, and a small human-blind classifier that flags hallucination patterns seen in past regressions.

Key metric table (selected, aggregated) — numbers are median across prompts and seeds:
- Instr-suite token edit distance (baseline=0): B(Flash) +2.1%, C(Paged KV) +0.4%, D(Cont-Batch) +0.9%, E(combined) +3.5%
- Retrieval exact-match: baseline 92.4% -> B 91.9% (-0.5), C 88.8% (-3.6), D 92.0% (-0.4), E 87.6% (-4.8)
- Long-gen truncation-rate: baseline 0.6% -> B 0.7%, C 0.8%, D 1.4% (high-concurrency), E 1.9%
- Latency p50 (long context): baseline 320ms -> B 245ms (-23%), C 310ms (-3%), D 300ms (-6%), E 220ms (-31%)

Representative diffs (human-curated):
1) Instr-suite example (short):
 Prompt: "Summarize the following and list action items: ..."
 Baseline output excerpt: "Action 1: Validate data pipeline; Action 2: Schedule weekly sync; Action 3: Add schema check."
 Flash output excerpt: "Action 1: Validate data pipeline; Action 2: Schedule weekly sync; Action 3 Add schema check."
 Observed delta: missing colon after "Action 3"; downstream parsing rules treat this as a separate bullet -> failing strict validator. Manual inspection: tokenization boundary shifted: colon was assigned to previous token under baseline but merged differently with flash kernels.

2) Retrieval-anchor example:
 Prompt: "Given items: B7, C9, D3 — which was last?"
 Baseline: "D3"
 Paged-KV: "C9"
 Notes: Off-by-one in recency; appears when retrieval items span a page boundary during attention read.

3) Long-narrative example (truncation):
 One run under cont-batch at high concurrency truncated at token ~1024 in 2/300 runs. Failure mode: batching queue delayed final KV flush causing scheduler to preempt the generation and return an end-of-stream.

Triage notes and root cause worklog:
- FlashAttention investigation: kernel numerics pass stress tests. We instrumented softmax inputs for ambiguous tokens; found small differences in pre-softmax logits (mean delta 1e-3) for tokens near probability tie. For deterministic decoders that pick argmax, that difference is enough to flip in ~2% cases. Patch idea: add a deterministic tie-breaker in post-softmax stage for instruction-family decodes.
- Paged KV: added unit test that simulates page boundary crossing during attention read. Reproduced the off-by-one within the pager logic (index floor/ceil mismatch when offset % page_size == 0). Proposed fix: normalize page offset using safe-mod and add regression unit tests.
- Continuous batching: traced scheduler timeline and found rare race where batch flush interval aligns with generation tail and the eviction callback runs early. Mitigation: add a backpressure token lock for in-flight KV frames and extend timeout window for tail-of-stream flushing.

Risk assessment and rollout recommendation:
- FlashAttention: benefits large (latency), risk moderate (minor token-level flips). Recommend gated rollout: enable for inference-only customers by default, opt-in for instruction-sensitive onboarding until tie-breaker patch deployed. Add post-deploy eval suite that samples instruction-suite at 0.1% of traffic.
- Paged-KV: benefits medium (memory), risk medium-high for retrieval use cases. Blocked for tenants using retrieval-heavy routes until pager fix merged and unit tests added. For customers using pinned model versions and retrieval, we should default to single-page mode.
- Continuous batching: benefits cost; risk operational. Recommend opt-in with guardrails: max-concurrency threshold, longer tail flush timeouts, and runtime metric alarms for truncation-rate >0.5%.

Immediate action items (owner):
- Aisha: push unit test and pager fix branch (PR: linked).
- Marco: implement deterministic tie-breaker shim for flash kernels + perf-run to ensure no p99 regressions.
- Jin: add continuous-batch backpressure metrics and a toggle in the console for per-tenant opt-in.
- Sofia: expand post-deploy eval to cover retrieval exact-match and set up alerting on drift >2% vs baseline.

Appendix — short reproducibility steps:
1) Checkout: git@github.com:redwood/inference.git@pr/1245
2) Launch node: ./scripts/run-eval --model rdlw-13b-v1 --variant flash --suite instr-suite --seeds 5 --log-tokens
3) For paged-KV: run with --kv-paged --page-size 32k and use retrieval-anchor suite.
4) For cont-batch: simulate high concurrency: ./scripts/stress --concurrency 256 --mode cont-batch --suite long-narrative-gen

Open questions:
- Is the percent of affected tokens stable across quantized variants (int8)? Early signals show amplification in quantized runs for flash kernel — needs deeper study.
- Should we add an automated token-level rollback for production when instruction-suite regression exceeds threshold? Operational complexity vs safety tradeoff to evaluate.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the instr-suite small but representative — it's cheap and catches the subtle argmax flips.
- Pager fix should include synthetic tests crossing multiple page boundaries; I hit a similar bug in 2024 with a different pager.
- Coordinate with SRE for canary traffic split once PRs land.

End of journal entry.
